results.content: Donald Trump's popularity rebounded slightly in this week's Economist / YouGov Poll after his recent slump, but he remains deeply unpopular. This week's poll finds that 36% of Americans strongly or somewhat approve of Trump's job performance, and 57% disapprove — a net job approval of -21. That's an improvement for Trump from the week before, when 35% approved and 61% disapproved for a net approval of -26. results.content: Donald Trump’s approval rating has fallen to record or near-record lows, with support among middle-aged voters dropping sharply as economic concerns weigh heavily on his presidency. According to the Economist/YouGov poll conducted July 25-27, just 34% of U.S. adults approve of Trump’s job performance, tied for the lowest point of either his first or second term, while 62% disapprove, yielding a net approval rating of -28.
results.title: Trump approval rating hits record low, drops sharply among middle-aged voters

results.content:
Two August Economist/YouGov surveys showed Trump’s net approval (those who approve minus those who disapprove) improving by more than 10 points among the voter groups.

It comes ahead of the November midterm elections, when the president’s standing could influence Republican candidates competing for control of Congress.
